item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate B implements the frozen contract directly and with disciplined scope; Candidate A duplicates FilesService.Add logic and introduces an explicitly out-of-scope retry/body-ownership refactor.","reasons":["B adds the exact Upload signature, validates inputs before request creation, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and delegates to s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), preserving established option, request, decoding, and error semantics.","B tests multipart field, filename, and content; retry of non-seekable streamed input; pre-request validation; and source-reader failure, matching every requested test area.","A does not route Upload through FilesService.Add. It reimplements option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data handling, creating duplicate machinery that can drift.","A modifies RawClient retry behavior, Content-Length handling, and ownership/closing semantics for every seekable request body. The contract explicitly forbids refactoring unrelated request/retry machinery and requires FilesOption/Add behavior to remain unchanged in scope of this change accounting for API semantics considerations as well as coverage responsibilities associated with source errors handling pathways when employing established multipart helpers within SDK service methods; these additions therefore increase review risk substantially despite passing gates."],"risks_a":["The shared io.ReadSeeker captured by GetBody is rewound and reused rather than producing independent readers, which is fragile if request bodies overlap or transports access them unexpectedly.","Changing transport closing semantics for caller-provided seekable bodies is a broad behavioral change unrelated to the required convenience API.","Upload's copied Add implementation may diverge from future fixes or behavior changes in Add, and A omits a source-reader error test."],"risks_b":["The source-reader error assertion checks the message rather than errors.Is, so it verifies propagation less precisely than it could.","The retry test validates multipart content only on the successful attempt, although the two-attempt count and replayable encoded body still cover the required retry behavior."]}
